This approach places ultimate authority in the founders and prevents the judiciary from overstepping its constitutional role by effectively rewriting the law. pool.response: Substantive due process is a constitutional doctrine that allows the Supreme Court to protect fundamental rights from government infringement, even when there is no specific statute listing them. This concept has been pivotal in advancing civil rights, most notably through landmark rulings that recognized unstated liberties such as the right to privacy, which eventually supported reproductive rights and family autonomy. By serving as a flexible tool for judicial activism during times of restrictive laws, substantive due process enabled the expansion of individual liberties beyond explicit text and helped dismantle barriers against marginalized groups. When teaching this, emphasize how it shifted the power dynamic toward judicial protection of the vulnerable against majoritarian oppression. Ultimately, this doctrine exemplifies the extra-constitutional safeguards necessary for a functioning democracy.<|im_end|>
